title: Chromatin Remodeling and Transcription Factor Networks Drive Sarcoma Cell-State Plasticity and Therapeutic Vulnerabilities
content: Sarcoma cells can shift between proliferative, invasive, stem-like, and differentiation-associated states. This Review examines how transcription factors and ATP-dependent chromatin remodelers, including SWI/SNF, ISWI, CHD/NuRD and INO80/SWR1, contribute to these changes across sarcoma subtypes. It also discusses compensatory chromatin mechanisms, therapeutic resistance, and how molecular profiling and patient-relevant models may help guide more precise treatment strategies.
